SOCIAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should be done with profit from a school project? (1 mark)
   A. Share it secretly
   B. Agree together how to use it, for example to buy books
   C. Hide it
   D. Throw it away

2. Which disease can spread more easily in wet weather because mosquitoes breed in puddles? (1 mark)
   A. Sunburn
   B. Malaria
   C. Broken leg
   D. Toothache

3. Which clothing helps drivers to see you on a rainy day? (1 mark)
   A. Dark grey clothes
   B. Bright or reflective clothes
   C. Brown clothes
   D. Black clothes

4. Which county borders Uganda? (1 mark)
   A. Nyeri
   B. Busia
   C. Kitui
   D. Nairobi

5. Why do herders in dry areas not live crowded in one place? (1 mark)
   A. They do not use water
   B. They dislike roads
   C. They have no families
   D. They move with animals to look for water and grass

6. Which statement about culture is true? (1 mark)
   A. Every community's culture deserves respect
   B. Only one culture is right
   C. Culture never changes
   D. Culture is only about clothes

7. Which is a way to promote child rights in school? (1 mark)
   A. Hiding problems
   B. Bullying
   C. Making posters and songs on child protection
   D. Ignoring children with problems

8. Which of these actions harms a historic place? (1 mark)
   A. Writing on the walls
   B. Learning its story
   C. Picking up litter
   D. Sweeping the compound

9. Who brings medicine and equipment to hospitals? (1 mark)
   A. Only teachers
   B. Nobody
   C. Drivers and traders
   D. Only farmers

10. A group spent Ksh 600 and earned Ksh 500. What happened? (1 mark)
   A. A loss of Ksh 100
   B. A profit of Ksh 1,100
   C. A profit of Ksh 100
   D. No change

11. What is peace? (1 mark)
   A. A loud noise
   B. Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other
   C. A kind of food
   D. A game

12. How often are governors elected? (1 mark)
   A. Every twenty years
   B. Every month
   C. Every year
   D. Every five years

13. Two pupils want the same ball. What is a peaceful solution? (1 mark)
   A. Hide it
   B. Take turns to play with it
   C. Fight for it
   D. Break it

14. Who leads a sub-location? (1 mark)
   A. Assistant chief
   B. Speaker
   C. Governor
   D. President

15. On the county map in the lesson, the neighbour drawn on the right side is in which direction from the county? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. North
   C. South
   D. East

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Draw a simple chart showing three workers, what each gives, and what each needs. (3 marks)

17. Name the four cardinal points. (2 marks)

18. Give three ways in which the rainy season helps people. (3 marks)

19. Explain the difference between clustered and scattered settlement. (3 marks)

20. Describe how to draw a dot map showing population distribution in your county. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Agree together how to use it, for example to buy books
   Profit should be used openly and wisely.

2. B — Malaria
   Mosquitoes that spread malaria breed in standing water.

3. B — Bright or reflective clothes
   Bright and reflective clothes stand out.

4. B — Busia
   Busia is on the border with Uganda.

5. D — They move with animals to look for water and grass
   Herding needs large areas of pasture.

6. A — Every community's culture deserves respect
   We must respect all cultures.

7. C — Making posters and songs on child protection
   Awareness helps protect children.

8. A — Writing on the walls
   Writing on old walls spoils them.

9. C — Drivers and traders
   Transport workers carry goods to hospitals.

10. A — A loss of Ksh 100
   They spent more than they earned: 600 - 500 = 100.

11. B — Calm and harmony where people live safely and respect each other
   Peace is harmony and safety.

12. D — Every five years
   General elections are held every five years.

13. B — Take turns to play with it
   Taking turns is fair.

14. A — Assistant chief
   An assistant chief leads a sub-location.

15. D — East
   When north is at the top, the right side is east.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: farmer gives food and needs clothes; teacher gives learning and needs food; driver gives transport and needs repairs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct row.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: North, east, south and west.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two correct points, 2 marks for all four.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Crops grow, grass grows for animals, and rivers and tanks fill with water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clustered means homes are close together in a group, for example around a town. Scattered means homes are far apart from each other.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for a clear contrast.

20. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the county boundary. Decide how many people one dot stands for. Put more dots where more people live and fewer dots where few live. Add a title and key.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.
